title: The Choir of Ashvale
premise: Petra Winterbourne, a mercenary bound by oath to a god who has not spoken in a decade, keeps the ledgers of the Ashvale Guild, which trades in impossible things: borrowed years, stolen names, bottled grief. When a dying courier presses a map of the king's sleeping mind into Petra's hands, they learn the monarch is slowly being devoured by the thing wearing his crown, and that their silent god was silenced deliberately—by the crown itself. Hunted by the Guild's own enforcers and shadowed by Sable, a rival ledger-keeper whose loyalty Petra cannot afford to trust, they must carry the map through the city's buried cathedral to unbind the king before the thirteenth moon turns. In the end, Petra discovers the god's silence was a prison they themselves helped build in a memory that was taken from them, and they must choose between restoring the god and saving the king—paying for one truth with another, as the crown burns and the thirteenth moon rises on a kingdom that will never remember what it owed.
about_author: Oscar Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing sealed church records before turning to fiction, a debt his novels repay in full. He writes from a coastal town where the fog arrives on schedule, and claims he can hear choirs in it.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A quiet night balancing the Guild's accounts—years sold back to dying men, a name returned to a ghost—establishes Ashvale's economy of the impossible and Petra's careful invisibility. The beat is controlled melancholy; Petra touches an entry in their own hand they don't remember writing.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Salt Door
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A bleeding courier collapses into the Guild's salt door, pressing a wax-sealed map into Petra's hands and whispering 'thirteen turns' before dying mid-sentence. Guild enforcers arrive minutes too late. The beat is dread breaking through routine; Petra lies for the first time in ten years.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Show
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The map depicts the king's sleeping mind as a cathedral floor plan, but rooms shift when unobserved, and one chamber is labeled in Petra's own handwriting. The emotional beat is vertigo—the past reaching forward—and ends with Petra deciding not to report the map to the Guildmaster.

chapters.title: The God Who Stopped Answering
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with flashback. At their oath-shrine, Petra performs the nightly rite to their silent god and remembers the day the prayers stopped being answered. We learn mercenary oaths here bind literally: broken promises become physical wounds. Beat: grief disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: Sable Keeps Better Books
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Rival ledger-keeper Sable Vane notices a missing entry—a dead courier erased from the rolls—and begins her own quiet audit. Charming, ruthless, she suspects Petra. The beat is cat-and-mouse tension; Sable files a false report to buy herself time to hunt alone.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises Early
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. An astronomer in the Guild's debt confirms the moon's cycle has shortened; the deadline is real and closer than the map implied. Enforcers raid Petra's lodgings. Beat: panic sharpening into resolve; Petra flees across the rooftops with the map sewn into their coat lining.

chapters.title: Borrowed Years, Spent Freely
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable corners Petra in a debtors' tavern and offers partnership instead of betrayal—she wants the crown gone too, for reasons she won't name. Uneasy alliance forms over stolen wine. Beat: wary attraction; two liars agreeing to tell each other exactly one truth each.

chapters.title: The King Who Is Not Alone in His Head
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Using a forged writ, Petra gains a glimpse of King Aldric at court and sees the wrongness: his shadow bows a half-second late, and he mouths words no one speaks. Beat: horror and pity intertwined; Petra realizes the man is still in there, screaming politely.

chapters.title: Rooms That Move When You Look Away
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Petra and Sable test the map in the city's undercrofts and find its chambers correspond to real buried places—but each room they enter costs them a memory to open. Beat: mounting sacrifice; Sable loses the name of her hometown and pretends not to care.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The Guildmaster reveals he has known about the map all along and offers Petra everything: absolution, protection, their erased memories returned—if they surrender it. He implies the Guild built the crown's prison long ago. Beat: temptation; Petra refuses and becomes officially hunted.

chapters.title: Enforcers at the Cathedral Gate
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Pursued into the ruined cathedral above the undercrofts, Sable holds the gate alone against three enforcers, revealing combat skill and a brand on her wrist marking her as former Guild property. Beat: fierce loyalty revealed; she takes a wound protecting the map without being asked.

chapters.title: One Truth Each, As Promised
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Tending Sable's wound, Petra pays their promised truth: ten years ago, as a young mercenary, they helped seal something beneath the palace and let their god take the blame-memory. Sable pays hers: she is the dead courier's sister. Beat: intimacy forged in confession; trust becomes real.

chapters.title: The Choir That Sings Beneath
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Descending past the cathedral's drowned nave, they hear the source of the map's shifting rooms: a choir of the imprisoned, singing the king's mind into order—or into captivity. Beat: terrible beauty; the song includes a voice Petra recognizes as their god's.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown Wears Everything
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the map's central chamber they find the crown's occupant: a parasite of accumulated oaths, feeding on every vow sworn in the kingdom, wearing the king's face like a glove. It offers Petra their memories back in exchange for walking away. Beat: cold seduction; the offer is almost reasonable.

chapters.title: The Memory They Took From Me Was Mine
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, deep flashback unlocked by the choir's song. Full revelation: Petra didn't just help seal the thing—they wrote its first binding, as the god's chosen hand, and the god went silent to hide them from it. Beat: shattering self-recognition; every choice since has been a flight from this one.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn, First Hour
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The moon completes its cycle at dawn; the parasite begins consuming the king outright, and tremors shake the city as sworn oaths everywhere start to fray. Sable chooses to stay despite an open escape route. Beat: love stated plainly, finally, in the middle of catastrophe.

chapters.title: Unbinding the King
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The climax begins: Petra reaches the king's dreaming core while Sable holds the choir's song steady, rewriting the binding in the only ink that works—Petra's own blood-oath. Beat: desperate, sacrificial momentum; the god's silence finally breaks, answering with a single word: 'Remember.'

chapters.title: The Choice Between God and King
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The unbinding demands a price: restore the god fully and the king dies with the parasite; save the king and the god stays mute forever. Petra finds the third path—taking the binding into their own body. Beat: tragic transcendence; Petra chooses to become the prison.

chapters.title: Ashvale Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The crown burns, the king wakes weeping and free, and the city's collective memory of the crisis dissolves—as does most of what Petra was. Sable carries an unconscious Petra out through collapsing undercrofts. Beat: grief and tenderness; the rescuer now needs rescue.

chapters.title: Ledgers With Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, fragmented. Petra wakes with vast gaps—no guild, no god, no reason to distrust the red-haired woman watching over them. Sable begins writing down everything Petra lost, reading it aloud each morning. Beat: fragile hope; love rebuilding what duty consumed.

chapters.title: The Word the God Left Behind
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Among the recovered fragments is the god's last word—'Remember'—and Petra realizes some memories weren't taken but planted, seeds for exactly this ending. They choose which blanks to refill and which to leave empty. Beat: quiet agency; identity as authorship rather than inheritance.

chapters.title: A New Entry, In Our Own Hand
chapters.summary: Shared POV, closing chapter. Petra and Sable reopen the Guild under new rules—impossible things traded honestly, ledgers kept in two hands—and the freed king, remembering nothing, sends an anonymous donation. On the last page, Petra writes a new entry: their own name, willingly given. Beat: earned peace; the story ends where it began, but the hand holding the pen has changed.
